text: I've had this dry cough going on for about two months now. It doesn't bring up any phlegm or blood, but I do notice I get short of breath when I try to do physical work. text: Thank you for clarifying; the absence of orthopnea and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea makes acute heart failure less likely, though the ankle swelling is concerning. Given the two-month history of dry cough and exertional dyspnea, have you noticed any weight loss, night sweats, or a history of smoking?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I haven't lost any weight or had night sweats. Yes, I am a long-term smoker with a 20 pack-year history, and I work as a mechanic.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) with possible early cor pulmonale.
